summary: Polygon's staff ranks its top 50 video games of 2023, with an intro by Mike Mahardy arguing that 2023 was a year when games felt vibrant and genre-bending. Games released, substantially updated, or culturally relevant in 2023 were eligible, with a Nov. 30 cutoff. The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom takes first place, followed by Baldur's Gate 3 and Alan Wake 2, with entries covering everything from indie puzzlers to major franchise sequels and remakes.
one_line: Polygon's ranked list of the 50 best video games of 2023, topped by The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom and Baldur's Gate 3.
key_facts: Polygon's top 50 games of 2023 list was voted on by staff; eligible games were released in 2023, received substantial updates in 2023, or achieved renewed cultural relevance that year.
The eligibility cutoff was Nov. 30, the same as the previous year, so Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader and Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora are held for next year's consideration.
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, by Nintendo EPD for Nintendo Switch, is ranked #1, praised for Ultrahand and the Depths.
Baldur's Gate 3 by Larian Studios is #2, launched in August on PlayStation 5 and Windows PC; Polygon says its d20 'defined video game storytelling in 2023'.
Alan Wake 2 by Remedy Entertainment is #3, described as an 'assured masterpiece' and a 'hypertext mystery'.
Nintendo has three games in the top five: Tears of the Kingdom (#1), Super Mario Bros. Wonder (#4), and Pikmin 4 (#5).
Super Mario Bros. Wonder is the first side-scrolling 2D Mario platformer since New Super Mario Bros. U in 2012.
Armored Core 6: Fires of Rubicon by FromSoftware is #10; Street Fighter 6 by Capcom is #7, praised for World Tour mode and Modern Controls.
Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew (#18) is the final game of Mimimi Games, which announced its closure only two weeks after release.
Marvel's Midnight Suns (#22) was released in 2022 but narrowly missed the cutoff for the 2022 list, so it was eligible for 2023.
Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty (#15) and Patch 2.0 are credited with nearly erasing the memory of CD Projekt Red's botched 2020 launch.
Lies of P (#49) by Neowiz Games and Round8 Studio is called a Dark Souls-meets-Pinocchio game that feels like 'the genuine article' of Soulslikes.
Smaller and mobile titles also placed, including Connections (#31) from The New York Times, Suika Game (#43), and Subpar Pool (#37) by grapefrukt games.
